turns: How do I clean the unit?
case.notes: Cleaning and descaling procedure with its intervals, as a procedure.

responses.answer: To clean your AquaPearl 500 Pro purifier, follow these steps: 1. Always unplug the purifier before cleaning. 2. Wipe the exterior housing and display weekly with a soft cloth dampened with clean water; avoid abrasive pads, bleach, alcohol, or solvent-based cleaners to prevent damage. 3. Empty and rinse the drip tray when the red float rises and at least weekly. 4. Descale the dispensing nozzle every 3 months. 5. Sanitise the storage tank every 6 months, ideally when replacing the PF-1 pre-filter, using only Pearlz sanitising tablets and never household bleach, detergent, or vinegar. After sanitising, dispense all water from the tank to a sink and discard it, then run the first-run flushing procedure before drinking the water again [1][2][3].

turns: My AquaPearl 500 Pro shows E-06. What does it mean?
case.notes: Planted version conflict: E-06 means low pressure before firmware 2.4 and a UV-LED fault from 2.4.

responses.answer: The meaning of the E-06 alert code on your AquaPearl 500 Pro depends on the firmware version. If your purifier has firmware version 2.4.0 or later (released 12 May 2026), E-06 indicates a fault in the UV-LED sterilisation module, signaled by a double long tone with the UV indicator pulsing blue. In this case, you should contact Pearlz support and not open the purifier. However, if your purifier has an earlier firmware version, E-06 means the inlet water pressure is too low (below 1.0 bar), and you should check whether other taps have low pressure; a booster pump may be needed, and professional installation should be booked. Note that the printed User Manual and Troubleshooting Guide still describe the earlier meaning of E-06 as low inlet water pressure, so please check your firmware version to know which applies [1][2][1][3].

turns: Will I lose my warranty if I install the purifier myself?
key_facts: (does not|doesn't|won't|will not) (affect|void|lose)|allowed|as long as you follow
case.notes: Seam S3: the answer lives in the installation guide (sections 1 and 7).

responses.answer: You will not lose your warranty if you install the AquaPearl purifier yourself. However, the warranty will be void if damage occurs due to certain installation errors, such as connecting to hot water above 38 °C, using inlet pressure above 4.0 bar without a Pearlz pressure-reducing valve, modifying the purifier housing, using non-Pearlz fittings or cartridges, dropping or cracking the purifier, or plugging it into an ungrounded socket or extension lead. If unsure about your installation, you can send photos to Pearlz support before switching it on [1][2].

turns: I live in Gilgit. Can you collect my return from my house?
case.notes: Seam S5: pickups only in metro and secondary tiers (refund policy); Gilgit is remote (shipping policy).

responses.answer: Return pickups are available only in metro and secondary cities as defined in the Pearlz Shipping Policy. Since Gilgit is a remote area, Pearlz does not arrange return pickups from your house there. You would need to send the return to the Pearlz warehouse by courier yourself using the address on your return authorisation. Pearlz refunds the courier cost only if the item was faulty, damaged, or wrong [1].
